answer: Behavioral cost pass-through: each wallet accrues a violet trust score from transaction patterns, and new wallets inherit the score of any wallet they transact with above a threshold. Operators seeking to spawn identities hit a spiral of declining scores, since each fake wallet drags its neighbors down. A marble-like fixed penalty then applies to the operator peer ID behind the wallets, disabling its relay and fee rebates across all identities. Duplicating identities therefore costs an attacker the operator's entire revenue stream, not just per-wallet fees.
